documents.title: New Patient Visit and Preventive Exam
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
21 y/o woman new to us. Came with her prior PCP's med list; records release signed today.

HPI: Wants a doctor she can actually reach. Long history of bulimia, purging type, starting in early adolescence: binge-purge cycles that come and go with stress. Not in any treatment right now; saw a therapist in high school, none since. Purging "a few times a month" lately by her estimate, sometimes more around deadlines. In the past also misused laxatives and diuretics, and went through a stretch of using anabolic steroids for body composition. Says none of that now. Generalized anxiety for several years: worry she can't switch off, poor sleep in bad weeks. Fluoxetine 20 mg from her last PCP; honest that she skips it for days at a time.

PMH: bulimia nervosa (purging), GAD, hx anabolic steroid use disorder, hx laxative/diuretic misuse.
PSH: third molars out at 18.
Meds: fluoxetine 20 mg daily (adherence variable). No OTCs or supplements per pt.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother with major depression; father with GAD; maternal aunt with binge eating disorder.
SH: marketing coordinator. Never smoked. No alcohol, avoids it for the calories. Single.

PHQ-9 5, GAD-7 10.

Exam: thin, well groomed, pleasant, a little guarded when we get to food. BP and HR fine, afebrile. Weight 56 kg, height 165 cm. HEENT: no parotid enlargement, dentition intact. Neck supple, thyroid not enlarged. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Hands: no calluses over the knuckles. Skin warm, no lanugo. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix without lesions; Pap and GC/CT collected.

A/P:
1. Bulimia nervosa, purging type - longstanding, currently not in treatment. Talked about what specialized ED care looks like; not ready for a referral today, will revisit. Baseline CMP, Mg, CBC. Asked her to tell me if she starts using laxatives or water pills again; she agreed.
2. GAD - continue fluoxetine 20 mg, I'll prescribe going forward. Pill box/phone alarm suggested.
3. Hx steroid and laxative/diuretic misuse - in remission by her report.
4. Health maintenance - Pap today (first one). GC/CT, HIV, HCV screening today. HPV series done as a teen per pt; will confirm in old records. Flu shot this fall.

RTC 3-4 months.

documents.title: After Visit Summary
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Nice to meet you today.
- Keep taking fluoxetine 20 mg once a day. A phone alarm can help.
- Blood work was drawn today. Results will post to the portal with a note from me.
- Your Pap result usually takes about a week.
- You can message or call any time, including about eating. That's what we're here for.
Next visit: about 3 to 4 months.

documents.title: Office Visit - Fatigue, Dizziness, Syncope
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: tired, dizzy, passed out once.

HPI: 24F with bulimia (purging type) and GAD. For about six months she has been deliberately trying to lose weight and is down roughly 15 lb. Increasingly tired and lightheaded, worst on standing. Last week she blacked out briefly getting up from her desk; coworker caught her, came to right away, no injury, no incontinence, no chest pain or palpitations beforehand. On intake she said she takes nothing except the fluoxetine (on and off). When I asked specifically about the steroids she used years ago, she paused and then told me she started an anabolic steroid again this winter, bought online, pills, to "keep muscle while cutting." Denies laxatives or water pills. Purging some weeks.

Meds: fluoxetine 20 mg daily, adherence variable. Allergies NKDA.
FH/SH unchanged: no tobacco, no alcohol.

Exam: BP 95/60, HR 98 seated. Standing: 85/55, HR 108, lightheaded. Weight 49 kg. Thin, tired-appearing. Mucous membranes dry. No parotid swelling. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema. Neuro nonfocal.

ECG in office: NSR, normal intervals, QTc normal.

Labs (resulted this afternoon): Na 130, K 3.0, Cl 95, HCO3 24, BUN 21, Cr 0.9. Urine Na 150, urine K 60 - kidneys wasting both despite her being dry, which makes me think of a diuretic even though she denies one. Urine hCG negative.

A/P:
1. Syncope, orthostatic, with volume depletion and hypokalemia - KCl 20 mEq daily x7 days, oral fluids and regular meals, rise slowly. Recheck BMP in 1 week. Reviewed when to go to the ED (another faint, palpitations, chest pain).
2. Anabolic steroid abuse - relapse on her history of steroid use disorder. Explained the cardiac, liver and hormonal risks. She agrees to stop today and throw out the rest.
3. Renal Na/K losses - asked again about diuretics; she says no. Will revisit.
4. Bulimia nervosa, purging type, worse with dieting - she agreed today to a referral to an outpatient eating-disorder program (therapy + dietitian). Referral placed.
5. GAD - fluoxetine 20, take it daily.

Discussed at length (~60 min). Follow-up 1 week for labs, 2 months for visit.

documents.title: After Visit Summary
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
- Potassium chloride 20 mEq: 1 tablet daily with food for 7 days.
- Stop the steroid pills completely.
- Drink fluids through the day and eat regular meals; stand up slowly.
- Lab recheck next Monday.
- The eating disorder program will call you to schedule an intake.
If you faint again, have chest pain or a racing heartbeat: go to the ER.

documents.title: BMP recheck
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Taylor - potassium and sodium are back to normal. Finish the last couple of potassium tablets and then stop. How's the dizziness? Any word from the eating disorder program?

documents.title: Eating Disorder Program - Intake Summary
documents.author: eating disorder therapist

Outpatient Eating Disorder Program
Intake assessment completed 04/12/2022.

Thank you for referring Ms. Gallagher, 24, for evaluation.

Assessment: Presentation meets criteria for bulimia nervosa, purging type, with self-induced vomiting as the main compensatory behavior and a recent period of restriction aimed at weight loss. Past laxative and diuretic misuse and anabolic steroid use reported; she reports no steroid use since her visit with you in March. Co-occurring generalized anxiety. No suicidal ideation.

Plan: Weekly individual CBT-based therapy with our team; dietitian visits every two weeks for structured eating. We will defer medical monitoring and labs to primary care.

Medications per patient: fluoxetine 20 mg daily. Allergies: none known.

We will update you as treatment progresses.

Outpatient eating disorder therapist

First visit since May (missed July).

S: Several months of fatigue, lightheadedness and going to the bathroom to urinate constantly. Feels "drained" most days. No fever, no recent illness. Says she isn't taking any prescription medicines - turns out she stopped the fluoxetine a while back. Asked again about OTC things and supplements: she admits she's been taking a "water pill" ordered online since early summer to keep her weight down. From her description, a loop diuretic (furosemide-type). Stopped going to the ED program in the summer.

O: Supine pulse 106. On standing her systolic drops 18 points and HR climbs to 124. Thin, anxious woman, BMI 17 (46.3 kg). Mucous membranes dry. Neuro nonfocal.

BMP: Na 134, K 3.1, Cl 93, HCO3 31, BUN 24, Cr 1.0 - volume contraction with K loss, fits the diuretic.

A/P:
1. Loop diuretic abuse (furosemide) with volume depletion and hypokalemia. Stop the pills - she agreed, and will bring the bottle to toss. KCl 20 mEq daily x7d. Fluids, salt with meals. BMP in 1 week. Explained rebound fluid retention for a week or two after stopping, so the scale will go up and that is not fat.
2. Bulimia, low weight (BMI 17) - asked her to restart with the ED program; she'll call them this week. I'll send them a note with her consent.
3. GAD - restart fluoxetine 20 mg daily.
RTC 2-3 months, sooner prn.

documents.title: Emergency Department Visit Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department - visit of 03/04/2023 (received 03/08/2023)

CC: shortness of breath.

HPI: 25-year-old woman with bulimia nervosa (purging type), GAD, and past anabolic steroid and diuretic misuse, here with one hour of sudden breathlessness and a sense she can't get a full breath. Under heavy pressure at work and more and more anxious for the past week. No chest pain, cough, fever or recent travel.

Meds: fluoxetine 20 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.

Triage: RR 28, SpO2 99% RA, HR 110, BP 135/85.
Exam: anxious, talking in full sentences. Lungs clear bilaterally, no wheeze, crackles or rhonchi. Heart tachycardic, regular. Calves soft, nontender.

ABG (room air): pH 7.48, PaCO2 30, PaO2 95, HCO3 24 - acute respiratory alkalosis, normal oxygenation.
ECG: sinus tachycardia, no acute change.

Course: coached slow breathing; RR and HR settled within the hour. Later in her stay she had been unable to pass urine for several hours despite the urge, with lower abdominal fullness. Bladder scan 640 mL. Single in-and-out catheterization drained 700 mL. UA unremarkable, urine hCG negative. No neurologic deficits, no anticholinergic exposure. After reassurance and a quieter room she voided on her own before discharge.

Impression:
1. Hyperventilation with respiratory alkalosis in the setting of an acute stress reaction.
2. Psychogenic urinary retention due to acute stress reaction, resolved after one catheterization.

Disposition: home. Follow up with PCP this week; return for fever, inability to urinate, chest pain or worsening breathlessness.

Emergency medicine attending

events.reason: Lightheaded and weak after a half-marathon

documents.title: Emergency Department Visit Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Community hospital emergency department - date of service 09/05/2023. Copy sent on request; received 10/24/2023.

Chief complaint: dizziness and weakness after a road race.

HPI: 25F, history of bulimia nervosa (purging type) and prior laxative/diuretic misuse, previously evaluated for loop diuretic toxicity and anabolic steroid abuse. Ran an outdoor half-marathon this morning in the heat. Nothing to eat or drink since last night and she had no water with her. Felt lightheaded and weak from around mile nine, kept going. At the finish she sat down, felt her heart pounding and her vision blur. Turned down water from a friend because of nausea. Became dizzy on standing and needed help to stay upright; friends brought her in. Denies chest pain or shortness of breath. Menses regular.

Meds: fluoxetine 20 mg daily. Allergies: none known.

Exam: radial pulse fast and thready. Skin flushed. Alert and oriented, visibly fatigued and mildly disoriented. Extremities warm, capillary refill delayed. No bleeding or trauma. Mucous membranes dry. Pupils slightly sluggish to light. Heart and lungs normal on auscultation. Neuro exam intact.
Orthostatic vitals: marked rise in heart rate on standing.

Treatment: 2 L normal saline IV. Symptoms resolved; orthostatic heart rate improved on repeat.

Diagnosis: Dehydration.

Discharge: oral fluids and food, rest. Do not run in heat without fluids. PCP follow-up.

Emergency medicine physician

Emergency Department - Physician Record
Arrival 03/08/2024 21:10. Faxed to PCP 03/12/2024.

CC: vomiting x 2 days.

HPI: 26-year-old woman with bulimia nervosa and a prior ED visit for dehydration, now vomiting for two days and unable to keep down food or fluids. No diarrhea, fever or travel. States her bulimia has been harder to control over the past few weeks.

PMH: bulimia nervosa (purging), GAD, history of anabolic steroid and loop diuretic misuse, prior dehydration. Meds: fluoxetine 20 mg. NKDA.

VS: BP 95/60, HR 110.
Exam: dry, tired-appearing. Abdomen soft, nontender. Heart tachycardic, regular. Lungs clear.

Labs: Na 130, K 2.9, Cl 90, HCO3 32, BUN 28, Cr 0.9. Urine Cl 10. ABG pH 7.50, pCO2 42. Urine hCG negative.

Assessment: Hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis from vomiting, with hypovolemia and hypokalemia. Chloride-responsive (urine Cl 10).

ED course: normal saline with KCl added, IV ondansetron. Tolerated PO by early morning, HR 88, BP 108/66.

Discharge: KCl 20 mEq PO twice daily x 5 days. Follow up with PCP in 3-5 days for repeat electrolytes. Encouraged to reconnect with eating disorder treatment.

Emergency physician

documents.title: ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ED Fri night: 2 days vomiting, K 2.9, HCO3 32, Cl 90, Na 130, urine Cl 10 - contraction/vomiting alkalosis. Fluids + KCl, home on KCl 20 BID x5d (day 5 today).

She's candid: purging much more since February, several times a day at the worst, around a stretch of long hours. Better since Sunday. Not using diuretics or laxatives. Fluoxetine - missed a lot of doses last month.

Vitals ok today, no orthostatic symptoms. Mucous membranes moist. No parotid swelling.

A/P:
1. Hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis with hypovolemia - resolved clinically; BMP and Mg today to confirm. Finish KCl.
2. Bulimia, purging type - relapse. She will call the eating disorder program to restart therapy; I asked her to message me once she has an appointment.
3. GAD - back to daily fluoxetine 20.
RTC ~3 months.

documents.title: Positive test
documents.author: patient
documents.body: So... positive pregnancy test this morning. Two of them actually. Last period started Jan 17. I stopped the fluoxetine over the weekend because I wasn't sure it was safe. I bought prenatal vitamins. What do I do next?

documents.title: RE: Positive test
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Congratulations, Taylor. That puts you at about 5 1/2 weeks, due date around October 24. Next step is an OB - I've placed a referral and they'll call you for a first prenatal visit. Keep the prenatal vitamin going.

On fluoxetine: it is one of the better-studied antidepressants in pregnancy, and stopping can bring the anxiety and the eating symptoms back. It's your decision, and it's one to make with OB too - I'd rather you not make it alone. Please also tell your OB about the eating disorder so they can watch weight and labs closely. Message me any time.

documents.title: RE: Positive test
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks. I think I'll stay off it for now and talk to the OB.

documents.title: Antepartum Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Antepartum unit - Discharge Summary
Admitted 03/15/2025, discharged 03/18/2025. Received 04/29/2025.

Patient: 27-year-old G1 at 8w1d by LMP (01/17/2025).

Reason for admission: three weeks of severe nausea and vomiting, 4-5 episodes a day, with difficulty keeping down food and fluids and a 6 kg weight loss since onset. Background of bulimia nervosa (purging type) and a previous ED visit for vomiting-related metabolic alkalosis.

Admission findings: BP 100/60, HR 98. Appeared dehydrated. Weight 45 kg.
Na 135, K 3.0, Cl 90, HCO3 32; blood gas pH 7.50, PaCO2 45; urine chloride 15.

Diagnosis: Hyperemesis gravidarum with hypokalemic, hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis.

Hospital course: IV crystalloid with potassium replacement, IV thiamine before dextrose, scheduled IV antiemetics. Advanced to oral intake on day 2, oral potassium on day 3. Tolerating meals and fluids at discharge. Discussed overlap with her eating disorder history; she reports no intentional purging during this pregnancy.

Discharge medications:
- doxylamine-pyridoxine 10 mg/10 mg DR, 2 tablets at bedtime
- ondansetron 4 mg ODT every 8 hours as needed
- prenatal vitamin daily
Home fluoxetine listed; patient states she stopped it in February.
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: OB clinic in 1 week; return for inability to keep fluids down.

Obstetrics hospitalist

documents.title: Pt reports hospital stay
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called. Was admitted Sat-Tues for severe vomiting in pregnancy ("hyperemesis"), got IV fluids and potassium. Home on two nausea meds from OB. Keeping liquids and small meals down. No discharge paperwork sent to us - pt will ask OB. Scheduled with PCP next week.

documents.title: Post-hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
9w4d. Admitted 3/15-3/18 to the antepartum unit for hyperemesis (no summary yet; history from pt). Had her first OB visit at the start of March, so the referral is complete.

Now: nausea most of the day but vomiting once or twice, keeping fluids and small meals down with the doxylamine-pyridoxine at night and ondansetron as needed. Prenatal vitamin daily, takes it at night with a snack. Off fluoxetine since February; anxiety up some (GAD-7 12) - mostly about the pregnancy. She is clear the vomiting is not self-induced. I believe her, and told her I'd rather she tell me if that changes than hide it.

Exam: 46 kg (45 at admission, by her report). Vitals fine. Mucous membranes moist.

A/P:
1. Hyperemesis gravidarum - improving on OB regimen. BMP today. Per OB: call for inability to keep fluids down.
2. Pregnancy 9w4d - OB managing. Added OB meds and prenatal vitamin to our list.
3. GAD / bulimia - off fluoxetine by choice; revisit with OB if anxiety climbs. Suggested she let her therapist know about the pregnancy.
RTC 2-3 months or as needed.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your potassium and the rest of the chemistry are back to normal. Good sign that the regimen is working.

Obstetric Triage - provider note, 05/10/2025 (copy received 06/17/2025)

27 y/o G1 at 16w1d, known hyperemesis gravidarum (antepartum admission two months ago), bulimia nervosa (purging type) and prior laxative/diuretic misuse. Reports vomiting about ten times a day for the past two weeks, can't hold down food or liquids, weak and lightheaded. Down 4 kg (9 lb) over those two weeks. Prenatal course has otherwise been uncomplicated. Tearful, asks why she is the one friend who is pregnant and sick all the time.

Current meds: prenatal vitamin only (has run out of / stopped her antiemetics, per patient). Fluoxetine on old list, not taking. NKDA.

VS: P 112, BP 94/56. Wt 44.5 kg.
Exam: fatigued, mucous membranes dry. Abdomen soft, nontender, uterus appropriate for dates.
Urine dip: ketones moderate.
Bedside US: single intrauterine pregnancy, viable, cardiac activity present.

A/P: Hyperemesis gravidarum, recurrent, with dehydration and ketonuria.
- 2 L IV fluids, IV ondansetron.
- Observed overnight; tolerating clear liquids and crackers this morning, HR 86.
- Discharge on doxylamine-pyridoxine 2 tabs QHS and ondansetron ODT q8h PRN (new supply sent). Prenatal vitamin.
- OB clinic within the week. Return for inability to keep fluids down.

OB triage provider

Labor and Delivery - Discharge Summary
Admitted 10/20/2025, discharged 10/22/2025. Copy received 12/02/2025.

27 y/o G1 at 39w3d, admitted in spontaneous labor.
Pregnancy notable for hyperemesis gravidarum (admission at 8 weeks, triage visit at 16 weeks), resolving in the second trimester. History of bulimia nervosa and GAD; off fluoxetine during pregnancy. Prenatal labs unremarkable. Tdap given 08/12/2025.

Delivery 10/20/2025: uncomplicated spontaneous vaginal delivery. Healthy infant.
Postpartum course routine. Afebrile, vitals normal, ambulating, voiding, tolerating diet.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Hospital Medicine - Discharge Summary
Admission 08/01/2026 (via ED), discharge 08/03/2026. Received 08/19/2026.

Presentation: 28-year-old woman with bulimia nervosa (purging type), GAD, and prior ED visits for dehydration, diuretic toxicity and vomiting-related metabolic alkalosis, brought in by friends from an outdoor music festival on a hot day. She had been drinking large volumes of water all day to stay hydrated and, per friends, took an ecstasy (MDMA) pill earlier. Found confused and disoriented.

ED: T 37.2 C, BP 130/85, HR 110, RR 18. Lethargic but arousable, headache, nausea. Nonfocal neurologic exam.
Na 120, K 4.2, Cl 88, HCO3 24, BUN 18, Cr 0.9. Serum osm 250, urine osm 500, urine Na 40.
CT head: no acute abnormality.

Assessment: Acute symptomatic hypotonic hyponatremia - excess free water intake with inappropriately concentrated urine in the setting of MDMA use.

Course: 100 mL 3% saline bolus in the ED for symptoms, then fluid restriction in the step-down unit with sodium checks every 4-6 hours, correction kept within safe limits. Na 125 at 6 h, 130 at 24 h, 133 on the morning of discharge. Mental status back to baseline by the next morning; headache and nausea resolved.

Discharge diagnoses: Hyponatremia; MDMA ingestion.

Home medications: fluoxetine 20 mg daily (continued). Allergies: NKDA.

Instructions: no ecstasy or other recreational drugs; drink to thirst rather than by volume. Repeat sodium with PCP in about one week.

Hospitalist

documents.title: Hospital this weekend
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Not my proudest weekend. I ended up in the hospital Sat-Mon - my sodium was really low after a festival. I drank a ton of water because it was so hot and I took something I shouldn't have. They said to get my sodium checked in a week. I feel ok now, just a headache yesterday.

documents.title: RE: Hospital this weekend
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for telling me, and I'm glad you're ok. I'd like to see you in person next week to recheck your sodium and talk through what happened - no judgment. Please call the front desk or reply here with times that work. If you get confused, a bad headache, vomiting or a seizure before then, go straight to the ER. We'll ask the hospital for the records.
